en.before: Three findings that cannot stand, and the reason for each. **"Annex B requires X"** - Annex B is written in `should` and B.1 says it is not always suitable or sufficient. **"The organization must justify departing from Annex B"** - B.1 states expressly that organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability. **"Annex B is informative so it is irrelevant"** - it is normative, and clause 6.1.3 e) obliges consideration of it.
en.after: Three findings that cannot stand, and the reason for each. **"Annex B requires X"** - Annex B is written in `should` and B.1 says it is not always suitable or sufficient. **"The organization must justify departing from Annex B"** - B.1 states expressly that no organization has to document or justify including or excluding implementation guidance in its statement of applicability. **"Annex B is informative so it is irrelevant"** - it is normative, and clause 6.1.3 e) obliges consideration of it.

en.before: **The anomaly**, stated so no item turns on it: Note 2 to entry under clause **3.26**, the definition of statement of applicability, contains `shall` - all identified risks and the risk management measures established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability. A `shall` inside a note to a definition is unusual drafting. Where the statement of applicability is at issue, **cite clause 6.1.3 f)**, which states the requirement in the requirement text and needs no argument about whether notes are normative.
en.after: **The anomaly**, stated so no item turns on it: Note 2 to entry under clause **3.26**, the definition of statement of applicability, contains `shall` - all identified risks and the risk management measures established to address them shall appear in the statement of applicability. A `shall` inside a note to a definition is unusual drafting. Where the statement of applicability is at issue, **cite clause 6.1.3 f)**, which states the requirement in the requirement text and needs no argument about whether notes are normative.

en.before: - **Two Table A.1 controls contain an internal `should`.** A.6.2.6 requires the organization to define and document the necessary elements for ongoing operation of the AI system, and states that at a minimum this **should** include system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support. A.6.2.8 requires the organization to determine at which life cycle phases event log record keeping **should** be enabled, but at the minimum when the AI system is in use. In each, the control obligation is the `shall` and the enumerated content is advisory.
en.after: - **Two Table A.1 controls contain an internal `should`.** A.6.2.6 requires the organization to define and document the necessary elements for ongoing operation of the AI system, and states that at a minimum this **should** cover monitoring of the system and its performance, repairs, updates and support. A.6.2.8 requires the organization to determine at which life cycle phases event log record keeping **should** be enabled, and in any case while the AI system is in use. In each, the control obligation is the `shall` and the enumerated content is advisory.

en.before: The provision at clause 4.2 is a **NOTE** - relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change. A note is neither a requirement nor guidance in the sense a `should` carries, and no finding rests on it. What it does is signal where the topic surfaces when interested-party requirements are determined under 4.2's actual requirements.
en.after: The provision at clause 4.2 is a **NOTE** - interested parties may have requirements that relate to climate change. A note is neither a requirement nor guidance in the sense a `should` carries, and no finding rests on it. What it does is signal where the topic surfaces when interested-party requirements are determined under 4.2's actual requirements.
